column1: # Live RBAC route matrix: Phase 3 (permissions). Each step adds the rows of the behaviour it
# changes; a row of an earlier file whose answer a step changes is tagged superseded-by:p3 there.
# Columns: id, since, actor, method, path, body, expect, tags (see tests/rbac_matrix_live.sh).
# ---- step 3.11: sets, overrides and admin profiles; hierarchy and no-escalation ----
# With RBAC_PERMISSIONS_ENABLED off the routes do not exist (404). With it on, rbac-admin-a is a
# Full admin (no profile: no admins:manage, no admin_profiles:manage, no instance:settings) and
# never Root, so every row that could change something is refused before any write: Root's
# powers (admin profiles, the instance default, another admin) answer root_only, a member answers
# 403 naming the permission, and the "allowed" rows send what the route refuses after its checks
# (an administration right in a member set or an override, a cross-tenant grant without the
# password, an unknown set, a built-in). The stateful flows (creating, editing, deleting, a
# removal signing the account out, admins:manage over a strict subset) are proved by the route
# tests of step 3.11 against the in-memory database.
# ---- step 3.12: /api/auth/me names the permissions in force ----
# Every account's answer carries `capabilities` (the ids can() decides with) and `flags`; under act-as a
# member permission counts only when both people hold it, an administration one is the admin's. With
# RBAC_PERMISSIONS_ENABLED on an admin's answer also names whom it acts as (`actingAs`), which is why
# baseline.tsv's bl-me-actas is superseded here by an off and an on row.
# ---- step 3.13: the sets a new account starts with ----
# `sets` on an invite or a create follows the assignment rules: a set holding an exploitation approval,
# sessions or Kali exec takes the creator's own password, an unknown set is refused. Nothing is
# created: the invite names an address already in use, which the switch-off twin answers (the key is
# ignored there, as any unknown key was), and the create is refused before its write. A creator
# without users:assign_permissions naming a set (no seeded admin profile is one) is proved by
# ---- step 3.16: the exit criteria of the permission engine ----
# One seeded account per built-in set (e2e-rbac-seed.mjs: analyst = Read-only analyst, operator = Recon
# operator, usermgr = an admin on User manager) is refused by the permission, or the rule, its body
# names; a switch-off twin keeps today's answer. Nothing is started or written: an allowed request is
# one the route refuses after its checks (a bogus mode, a missing field). A project the account cannot
# see answers 404 before any permission is weighed. The approval refusal itself happens on the agent
# socket (tests/rbac_approval_cap_live.sh, E2E P3-05): here, the permissions the ticket's cap is read
# from. A token call to start_recon is E2E P3-02/P3-06: the analyst cannot mint one at all, and a
# minted scope the owner cannot use is refused at the mint.
